checklist.text: Use a Scanner to read the item price (double) and the quantity (int).
Compute the subtotal as price times quantity.
Apply a 10% bulk discount to the subtotal when the quantity is 10 or more.
Add 7% sales tax to the discounted subtotal.
Print the Subtotal, Tax and Total lines with two decimal places.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named OrderTotal.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner to read an item price (double) and a quantity (int).
2. Computes the subtotal as price times quantity.
3. If the quantity is 10 or more, applies a 10% bulk discount to the subtotal.
4. Adds 7% sales tax to the discounted subtotal.
5. Prints three lines exactly like this, with two decimal places:
   Subtotal: $X.XX
   Tax: $X.XX
   Total: $X.XX
Use named constants for the tax rate, discount rate and bulk quantity, follow Java
naming conventions, and comment your code.

checklist.text: Prompt for and read hours worked and hourly pay rate as doubles.
Validate hours (0 to 80) and rate (greater than 0), re-prompting until valid.
Declare calculatePay above main, define it below main, and call it to compute gross pay.
Pay overtime at 1.5 times the rate for hours over 40.
Print exactly 'Gross pay: $X.XX' with two decimal places.

inputs.instructions:
Write a C++ program in a file named payroll.cpp that:
1. Prompts for hours worked and hourly pay rate (both doubles).
2. Validates input: hours must be between 0 and 80 and the rate must be greater
   than 0; re-prompt until valid.
3. Declares a function prototype double calculatePay(double hours, double rate)
   above main, defines it below main, and calls it to compute gross pay.
4. Pays overtime at 1.5 times the rate for hours over 40.
5. Prints exactly: Gross pay: $X.XX (two decimal places).
Use named constants, curly braces on every control structure, consistent indentation
and comments.

checklist.text: Use a Scanner to read one whole number.
Print Even for an even number and Odd for an odd number.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named EvenOdd.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner to read one whole number.
2. Prints Even if the number is even and Odd if it is odd.
Follow Java naming conventions and comment your code.

checklist.text: Use a Scanner to read the Fahrenheit temperature as a double.
Convert to Celsius with (F - 32) * 5 / 9, using a named constant for 32.
Print Celsius: X.X with one decimal place.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named FahrenheitToCelsius.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner to read a temperature in Fahrenheit (double).
2. Converts it to Celsius with the formula (F - 32) * 5 / 9. Use a named constant for 32.
3. Prints Celsius: X.X with one decimal place.
Follow Java naming conventions and comment your code.

checklist.text: Read exactly five int test scores with a Scanner in a for loop.
Reject a score below 0 or above 100 and ask for it again.
Compute the average of the scores as a double.
Count the scores that are 60 or higher.
Return the letter grade from a method letterGrade(double average).
Print the average with one decimal, the passing count and the letter grade.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named GradeBook.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner and a for loop to read exactly five test scores (int).
2. Rejects any score below 0 or above 100 by asking for that score again.
3. Computes the average of the scores as a double.
4. Counts how many scores are 60 or higher.
5. Has a method letterGrade(double average) that returns "A" for 90 or more, "B" for 80 to 89,
   "C" for 70 to 79, "D" for 60 to 69 and "F" otherwise.
6. Prints three lines: Average: X.X (one decimal), Passing scores: N, Letter grade: L.
Use named constants for the number of scores and the passing score, follow Java naming
conventions, and comment your code.

checklist.text: Prompt for and read the length and width as doubles.
Compute the area and the perimeter.
Print Area and Perimeter with two decimal places.

inputs.instructions:
Write a C++ program in a file named rectangle.cpp that:
1. Prompts for the length and width of a rectangle (both doubles).
2. Computes the area and the perimeter.
3. Prints Area: X.XX and Perimeter: X.XX with two decimal places.
Use consistent indentation and comments.

checklist.text: Prompt for and read the bill amount and the service rating.
Use a 20% tip for a rating of 3 and 15% otherwise, with named constants.
Print Tip: $X.XX with two decimal places.

inputs.instructions:
Write a C++ program in a file named tip.cpp that:
1. Prompts for the bill amount (double) and a service rating from 1 to 3 (int).
2. Uses a 20% tip for a rating of 3 and a 15% tip for any other rating. Use named constants.
3. Prints Tip: $X.XX with two decimal places.
Use curly braces on every control structure, consistent indentation and comments.

checklist.text: Read the price and quantity of four items in a for loop.
Validate price (greater than 0) and quantity (0 or more), re-prompting until valid.
Declare lineTotal above main, define it below main and call it for every item.
Give a 10% discount on a line total when the quantity is 12 or more.
Add up the grand total and count the discounted items.
Print Items discounted and Grand total with two decimal places.

inputs.instructions:
Write a C++ program in a file named inventory.cpp that:
1. Uses a for loop to read the unit price (double) and quantity (int) of four items.
2. Validates each entry: the price must be greater than 0 and the quantity 0 or more;
   re-prompt until valid.
3. Declares a function prototype double lineTotal(double price, int quantity) above main,
   defines it below main, and calls it for every item.
4. Gives a 10% discount on an item's line total when its quantity is 12 or more.
5. Adds up the grand total and counts how many items received the discount.
6. Prints Items discounted: N and Grand total: $X.XX (two decimal places).
Use named constants, curly braces on every control structure, consistent indentation and comments.

checklist.text: Use a Scanner to read a whole number n.
Print Invalid and stop when n is less than 1.
Add the numbers from 1 to n with a for loop and print Sum: X.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named SumToN.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner to read a whole number n.
2. Prints Invalid and stops when n is less than 1.
3. Otherwise uses a for loop to add the numbers from 1 to n and prints Sum: X.
Follow Java naming conventions and comment your code.

checklist.text: Use a Scanner to read the password as a String.
Use a loop to find at least one digit.
A password is valid with at least 8 characters and a digit; print Valid or Invalid.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named PasswordCheck.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner to read a password (String).
2. A password is valid when it has at least 8 characters and contains at least one digit.
   Use a loop to look for the digit.
3. Prints Valid or Invalid.
Follow Java naming conventions and comment your code.

checklist.text: Read prices into an ArrayList<Double> until the user enters 0.
Reject a negative price and ask again.
Return the sum of the prices from totalPrice(ArrayList<Double>).
Take 10% off in applyCoupon when the total is 100 or more.
Print Cart is empty when no price was entered.
Otherwise print Items, Total and Final with two decimal places.

inputs.instructions:
Write a Java program named ShoppingCart.java that:
1. Uses a Scanner to read item prices (double) into an ArrayList<Double> until the user enters 0.
2. Rejects a negative price and asks again.
3. Has a method totalPrice(ArrayList<Double> prices) that returns the sum of the prices.
4. Has a method applyCoupon(double total) that takes 10% off when the total is 100 or more.
5. Prints Cart is empty when no price was entered. Otherwise prints Items: N, Total: X.XX and
   Final: X.XX (two decimal places).
Use named constants for the coupon rate and the coupon minimum, follow Java naming conventions
and comment your code.
